extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and organizations wishing to comment on proposed federal regulations published in the Canada Gazette
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments on proposed federal regulations via the Canada Gazette consultation platform, including account choices, submission format, content limits, confidentiality options, and data protection considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account options and identity disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Users may create a new account (identifying as individual or organization), log in with an existing account, or submit comments anonymously without registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose account type deliberately: organization accounts will be associated with a public organization name, whereas individuals can submit with privacy protections or anonymously. Consider whether you want public accountability associated with an organizational submission or the privacy of an individual/anonymous submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and required entry of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be entered directly into text boxes on the consultation page; supporting documents may be attached but 'you must enter your comments in the commenting boxes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the online text boxes for substantive content; the platform allows saving drafts and editing prior to final submission. Relying solely on attachments is discouraged—typed content in the box is encouraged and necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment allowance and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting documents may be attached to a submission, but they do not substitute for entering comments in the provided commenting boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments are permitted as supplementary material; ensure core arguments and key points are placed in the comment box so they are visible and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication policy for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted comments are published online regardless of submission method (online, email, or mail). Personal names are kept confidential, but organization names are posted publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume your comment will be publicly accessible and archived; if representing an organization, be aware the organization name will appear publicly. Plan wording accordingly given public visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content restrictions — prohibited material
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments cannot include: personal information, classified government data, discriminatory language, hate speech, threats, external links, or other content violating Canadian laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include personal data or restricted/classified information. Avoid discriminatory or hateful language and threats. Remove external links and any content that could contravene Canadian law to prevent rejection or removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential business information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a dedicated text box for confidential business information (details not publicly available with economic value); such submissions will not be published if properly classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting economically sensitive information that qualifies as confidential business information, place it in the designated confidential box and clearly mark/classify it; follow any additional instructions to ensure it is treated as non-public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data protection and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal information is collected under the Financial Administration Act. Individual names are not posted online; comments remain posted for at least 10 years. Canadians have access and correction rights regarding their personal data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of privacy protections and legal basis for data collection. Expect a minimum 10-year public retention of comments and exercise access/correction rights if needed. Avoid including unnecessary personal data in the comment itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications for comment effectiveness (Canadian context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical considerations affecting how a comment may be received: organizational comments carry public accountability (names posted); individual comments enjoy privacy protection; the system encourages substantive content typed into the comment box; hate speech and discriminatory content will be rejected; comments form a long-term policy archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding how to frame and submit a comment, weigh public accountability vs privacy, prioritize substantive in-box content over attachments, avoid prohibited language, and recognize that comments contribute to a publicly accessible, long-term policy record (minimum 10 years).
